<h2>Description</h2>

<p>Computes the diffusive component of a gas flux for a single aquatic chamber
incubation. When bubbling events are present, only the portion of the time
series that precedes ebullition is used, so that abrupt bubble-driven steps
do not contaminate the diffusive slope. The retained window is then passed to
the <code>goFlux</code> / <code>best.flux</code> machinery,
which fits the linear (LM) and Hutchinson-Mosier (HM) models and selects the
best one according to <code>criteria</code>.
</p>


<h2>Usage</h2>

<pre><code class='language-R'>goAquaFlux.diffusive(
  df,
  gastype,
  criteria = c("MAE", "RMSE", "AICc", "SE", "g.factor", "kappa", "MDF", "nb.obs",
    "intercept", "p-value"),
  bubble_gas = "CH4dry_ppb",
  bubbles = NULL,
  minimum_window = 30,
  abrupt.window = 30,
  abrupt.min.points = 10,
  abrupt.threshold = 0.5
)
</code></pre>


<h2>Arguments</h2>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="df">df</code></td>
<td>
<p>A data.frame for a single incubation, as prepared by
<code>goAquaFlux</code>. Must contain <code>Etime</code> (starting at 0),
<code>flag</code>, the gas column named by <code>gastype</code>, the instrument
precision column (<code>*_prec</code>), <code>Vtot</code>, <code>Area</code>, <code>Pcham</code>,
<code>Tcham</code>, and (for non-water gases) <code>H2O_mol</code> and/or <code>H2O_ppm</code>.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="gastype">gastype</code></td>
<td>
<p>Character; name of the gas concentration column.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="criteria">criteria</code></td>
<td>
<p>Character vector of model-selection criteria passed to
<code>best.flux</code>. Defaults to the full goFlux criteria set.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="bubble_gas">bubble_gas</code></td>
<td>
<p>Character; the gas used to detect bubbles (typically
<code>"CH4dry_ppb"</code>). When <code>gastype == bubble_gas</code> the diffusive window
is always truncated at the first detected bubble. For other gases the
window is only truncated if a bubble coincides with an abrupt change in
that gas (see Details).</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="bubbles">bubbles</code></td>
<td>
<p>Data.frame of bubbling events from <code>find.bubbles</code>
(or <code>NULL</code>). Must contain a <code>start</code> column.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="minimum_window">minimum_window</code></td>
<td>
<p>Integer; minimum number of observations required in the
diffusive window. If fewer are available the function returns <code>NA</code>.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="abrupt.window">abrupt.window</code></td>
<td>
<p>Numeric; half-width (seconds) of the window used on each
side of a candidate bubble time when testing for an abrupt slope change
(non-bubble gases only). Default <code>30</code>.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="abrupt.min.points">abrupt.min.points</code></td>
<td>
<p>Integer; minimum points required on each side of the
candidate time to run the abrupt-change test. Default <code>10</code>.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="abrupt.threshold">abrupt.threshold</code></td>
<td>
<p>Numeric; relative slope-change threshold above which a
bubble is deemed to perturb the gas. Default <code>0.5</code> (i.e. 50%).</p>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h2>Details</h2>

<p>For the bubble gas itself, ebullition by definition perturbs the signal, so
the diffusive window ends at the first detected bubble. For other gases a
bubble does not necessarily perturb the concentration; the window is only cut
at the first bubble time that is accompanied by an abrupt change in local
slope (the ratio of the post- to pre-bubble slope exceeds
<code>abrupt.threshold</code>). If no such change is found, the full series is used.
</p>


<h2>Value</h2>

<p>A list with <code>flux</code>, <code>SE</code>, <code>n_used</code>,
<code>first_bubble_time</code> (the start of the first detected bubble, or
<code>NA</code>), <code>best.flux.output</code> (the full <code>best.flux</code> row) and,
when flux cannot be computed, a <code>message</code>.
</p>

</p>
